cross-bridge.short: The link a myosin head (muscle's motor protein) makes with actin (the filament it pulls on). Each attach–pull–detach cycle splits one ATP and moves the filaments a few nanometres.

fascicle.short: A bundle of muscle fibres wrapped in its own connective tissue sheath (the perimysium). A whole muscle is a bundle of fascicles.

muscle-fibre.short: One skeletal muscle cell: long, cylindrical and with many nuclei, packed with myofibrils. Up to about 100 μm wide and up to 30 cm long.

myofibril.short: A thread about 1.2 μm wide that runs the length of a muscle fibre, made of sarcomeres joined end to end. A fibre holds hundreds to thousands of them.

sarcomere.short: The repeating contractile unit of a myofibril, about 2 μm long, from one Z-disc to the next. It shortens when actin filaments slide past myosin filaments.

actin.short: The protein of the thin filaments in a sarcomere, anchored at the Z-discs. Myosin heads grab it and pull it towards the middle of the sarcomere.

myosin.short: The motor protein of the thick filaments in the middle of a sarcomere. Its heads bind actin and pull, splitting ATP each cycle.

z-disc.short: The thin plate at each end of a sarcomere that anchors the actin filaments and links one sarcomere to the next.

tendon.short: A tough, rope-like band of connective tissue joining muscle to bone. It passes on muscle force and, in running, stores and returns elastic energy like a spring.

atrium.short: One of the two upper, thin-walled chambers of the heart. The right atrium receives blood from the body, the left atrium from the lungs.

ventricle.short: One of the two lower, muscular pumping chambers of the heart. The right ventricle pumps to the lungs, the left ventricle to the rest of the body.

pulmonary-circulation.short: The circuit from the right ventricle through the lungs and back to the left atrium, where blood loads oxygen and unloads CO₂.

systemic-circulation.short: The circuit from the left ventricle through the aorta to every tissue and back through the great veins (venae cavae) to the right atrium.

coronary-arteries.short: The left and right arteries that branch off the aorta just as it leaves the heart and supply the heart muscle itself.

diastole.short: The relaxation phase of the heartbeat, when the chambers fill. Most coronary blood flow happens in diastole. Its opposite, the contraction phase, is systole.

capillary.short: The smallest blood vessel, linking the smallest arteries to the smallest veins. Its wall is so thin that gases, nutrients and wastes pass across it.

conducting-zone.short: The airways from nose and mouth down to the smallest tubes before the air sacs (terminal bronchioles). They carry, clean, warm and humidify air but exchange no gas.

anatomical-dead-space.short: The air in the conducting airways that never reaches the alveoli, so takes no part in gas exchange.

alveolus.short: A tiny air sac, about 200 μm across, at the end of the airways, wrapped in capillaries. The site of gas exchange; an adult lung has hundreds of millions.

surfactant.short: A soapy film of fats and proteins, made by type II cells in the alveoli, that lowers surface tension so the alveoli don't collapse.

respiratory-membrane.short: The wall between alveolar air and capillary blood: an alveolar cell, a thin supporting layer and a capillary cell, about 0.5 μm thick in all.

diaphragm.short: The dome-shaped muscle under the lungs and the main breathing muscle. Contracting, it moves down, enlarges the chest and draws air in.

plasma.short: The liquid part of blood, mostly water with about 7% proteins plus salts, nutrients and hormones. About 55% of blood volume.

haematocrit.short: The share of blood volume taken up by red cells: about 41% in women and 47% in men on average. Falls when plasma volume grows.

haemoglobin.short: The iron-containing protein that fills red cells. It has four protein chains, each with one iron-holding haem group, so one molecule carries up to four O₂.

haemoglobin-mass.short: All the haemoglobin in the circulation, in grams (or g·kg⁻¹ body mass). Unlike Hb concentration, it doesn't change when plasma volume does.

collagen.short: The body's main structural protein: tough, rope-like fibres that give tendons, ligaments and the wrappings around muscle their strength.

aorta.short: The body's main artery: the large vessel that leaves the left ventricle and branches to carry oxygen-rich blood to every tissue except the lungs.

anaemia.short: Too little haemoglobin in the blood to carry enough oxygen, from losing red cells or making too few (for example from low iron). It lowers endurance.
